==English== {{wp}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{l|en|eben}} {{qualifier|etymology 1: adverb, adjective}} * {{l|en|e'en}} {{qualifier|etymology 1: adverb, etymology 2: noun; contraction, poetic, archaic}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈiːvən/|[ˈɪi̯vən]|~|[ˈɪi̯vn̩]}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-even.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|iːvən|s=2}} * {{hyph|en|e|ven}} ===Etymology 1=== {{ety|en|id=flat|:inh|enm:even}} From {{inh|en|enm|even}}, from {{inh|en|ang|efn|t=flat; level, even, equal}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*ebn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*ebnaz}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*h₁émnos|*(h₁)em-no-|t=equal, straight; flat, level, even}}. Cognate with {{cog|stq|íeuwen||even, flat}}, {{cog|fy|even||even}}, {{cog|gsw|ëben||even}}, {{cog|cim|ébane||even}}, {{cog|nl|even||even, equal, same}}, {{m|nl|effen||leveled}}, {{cog|de|eben||even, flat, level}}, {{cog|da|jævn||even, flat, smooth}}, {{cog|is|jafn||even}}, {{cog|nb|jevn||even, smooth}}, {{cog|nn|jamn||even, smooth}}, {{cog|sv|jämn||even, level, smooth}}, {{cog|got|𐌹𐌱𐌽𐍃||even}}, {{cog|oco|eun||equal, right}} (attested in Vocabularium Cornicum {{m|oco|eun-hinsic||iustus, i. e., just}}), {{cog|obt|eun||equal, right}} (attested in Eutychius Glossary {{m|la|eunt||aequus, i. e., equal}}), {{cog|xbm|effn}}, {{cog|br|eeun}}, {{cog|sa|अम्नस्||tr=amnás|(adverb) just, just now; at once}}. The traditional proposal connecting the Germanic adjective with the root {{noncog|ine-pro|*h₂eym-}} ({{noncog|la|imāgō||picture, image, likeness, copy}}, {{noncog|la|aemulus||competitor, rival}}, {{noncog|sa|यम||tr=yamá|pair, twin}}) is problematic from a phonological point of view.Schaffner, Stefan (2000). “Altindisch ''amnás'', urgermanisch *''eƀna-'', kelt. *''eμno-''.” In: ''Indoarisch, Iranisch und die Indogermanistik. Akten des Kolloquiums der Indogermanischen Gesellschaft vom 2. bis 5. Oktober 1997 in Erlangen'', Forssman, Bernhard & Plath, Robert (eds.), Wiesbaden, pp. 491–505. In German. For the meaning development compare with {{m+|la|aequus||equal, level, even, flat, horizontal}}, {{m+|ru|ро́вный||even, level, flat, smooth}}, {{m|ru|ра́вный||equal}}, {{m|ru|по́ровну||in equal parts}}. ====Adjective==== {{en-adj|er,more}} # [[flat|Flat]] and [[level]]. #: {{ux|en|Clear out those rocks. The surface must be '''even'''.}} # Without great [[variation]]. #: {{ux|en|Despite her fear, she spoke in an '''even''' voice.}} # [[equal|Equal]] in proportion, quantity, size, etc. #: {{ux|en|The distribution of food must be '''even'''.}} #: {{ux|en|Call it '''even'''.}} # {{lb|en|mathematics|not comparable}} Of an [[integer]], [[divisible]] by [[two]]. #: {{ux|en|Four, fourteen and forty are '''even''' numbers.}} # {{lb|en|informal}} Of a [[number]], [[convenient]] for [[round#Verb|round]]ing other numbers to; for example, ending in a zero. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1989|author=w:Jerry Sterner|title=Other People's Money|section=act I |passage=Coles. How many shares have you bought, Mr. Garfinkle?
Garfinkle. One hundred and ninety-six thousand.{{...}}
Jorgenson. {{...}} How'd you figure out to buy such an odd amount? Why not two hundred thousand — nice '''even''' number. Thought you liked nice '''even''' numbers.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1998|author=w:Marya Hornbacher|title=[[w:Wasted: A Memoir of Anorexia and Bulimia|Wasted]]|chapter=8|year_published=1999|publisher=w:HarperPerennial|edition=paperback|isbn=0060930934|page=253|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=28iYykbTIhwC&pg=PA253&dq=even |passage=He put me on the scale in my underwear and socks: 82 pounds.{{...}} I left, humming all day long, remembering that once upon a time my ideal weight had been 84, and now I'd even beaten that. I decided 80 was a better number, a nice '''even''' number to be.}} # On [[equal]] [[monetary]] [[term]]s; neither [[owing]] nor being [[owed]]. # {{lb|en|colloquial}} On equal terms of a moral sort; [[quits]]. #: {{ux|en|You biffed me back at the barn, and I biffed you here—so now we're '''even'''.}} # [[parallel|Parallel]]; on a level; reaching the same limit. #* '{{RQ:KJV|Luke|xix|44|text=And
